verdict: The accepted version keeps the central claim but rebuilds its support. Trion regions are now traced from the metal-insulator transition in Rxx, the transport model states its assumptions and gives all four resistances, and an unsupported claim about quantum oscillations is replaced by a Lifshitz-Kosevich analysis. The abstract and outlook are softened and the electron-like Hall signal is credited to Coulomb drag. The old review's strongest concern, that excitons plus free carriers could give the same signals, is only partly met: no fit or discriminating test was added, and no artifact checks (antisymmetrization, leakage, excitation) or second Hall device appear.

inferred_requests.title: Show that the negative Hall signal needs trions, and give the full model
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely questioned whether the electron-like Hall signal in the hole layer proves a trion Hall effect, and asked for the model's assumptions and explicit expressions for all four measured resistances. The authors stated the perfect-drag assumptions, added a no-exciton limit with a counterflow explanation, gave Rxx, Rxy, Rxx,drag and Rxy,drag for both trion types, and reframed the abstract around Coulomb drag.

inferred_requests.title: Explain how trion regions are identified in each device
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely asked how the trion boundaries were drawn, since the old figures overlaid boundaries from a constructed diagram on data from three devices. The new version traces boundaries from the metal-insulator transition in Rxx, checks them against p = 2n and n = 2p, adds the Rxx temperature dependence to the main text, and states Delta per device.

inferred_requests.title: Explain why trion regions appear, expand and shift with B
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely asked why trion regions expand with field and how the field evolution affects the Hall data. The new version adds schematic phase diagrams, a field-induced-confinement explanation, the upward shift in Vb from valley Zeeman splitting, and Rxx vs B alongside Rxy vs B.

inferred_requests.title: Analyse the quantum oscillations in the trion region
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely challenged the claim that vertical oscillation stripes show exciton binding survives, or asked whether they are trion Landau levels. The authors removed the claim and added a temperature-dependent Lifshitz-Kosevich analysis giving a mass well below the trion mass.

inferred_requests.title: Justify the binding-energy baseline and estimate
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely asked how the 'expected threshold without interactions' was obtained. The authors replaced it with the measured 10 K threshold and added 10 K RC panels for both layers; the capacitance conversion is unchanged.

inferred_requests.title: Support the negative-trion assignment and its higher resistance
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely questioned the claim that holes in negative trions are more tightly bound. The authors replaced it with an argument based on exciton dissociation and added Rxx-based boundaries and a 10 K panel to the negative-trion RC figure.

inferred_requests.title: Justify treating bilayer MoSe2 as a monolayer
inferred_requests.text: A referee likely asked why the bilayer electron layer can be described with a monolayer valley picture. The authors added that high Delta confines electrons to the layer nearer the WSe2.

inferred_requests.title: Clarify the drag measurement circuit
inferred_requests.text: A referee may have asked how a.c. coupling and the bias were handled in the drag configuration. The authors described the transformer and potentiometer wiring to named electrodes.

inferred_requests.title: Show the density dependence of the crossover temperature and reproducibility
inferred_requests.text: Referees may have asked for support for the density-dependent ionization scale and whether it holds in other devices. The authors restated the claim against the Fig. 4c,d maps and added a sentence that other devices give the same order of magnitude, without data.

inferred_requests.title: Fix figure and text inconsistencies
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely flagged the line-cut voltage mismatch, the Fig. 4 caption sign-change claim, and Methods typos. These were corrected.

inferred_requests.title: Cite related theory on electron-hole bilayers
inferred_requests.text: A referee may have asked for citations of quantum Monte Carlo work on symmetric electron-hole bilayers; two De Palo et al. papers were added.

issue_status.reason: Model now explains the negative Rxy through drag and counterflow, and the abstract credits Coulomb drag, but no fit or discriminating test against excitons plus free carriers is given and 'unambiguously demonstrates' remains.
No antisymmetrization, plus/minus B data, out-of-phase components or admixture estimate added.
No leakage data; the model only says interlayer tunnelling is ignored.
Assumptions stated and explicit Rxx, Rxy, Rxx,drag, Rxy,drag given for both trion types, but the asymmetric trion blocks and lack of comparison with data remain.
The upward shift of trion regions in Vb with B is now acknowledged and Rxx vs B is shown, but no fixed-density or low-field Hall slope is added.
Boundary determination per device now explained (MIT tracing, capacitance check) and Delta given, but the Hall data still come from one device; 'other devices' are mentioned without data.
Density-dependent crossover is stated against the Fig. 4 maps, but the EI/exciton scale is not separated and the crossover-to-binding-energy mapping is not discussed.
The tighter-binding claim is replaced and a 10 K negative-trion panel added, but no negative-trion binding energy is given.
Only 'for small B fields' is added; no mobilities, omega_c tau or discussion of the insulating regime.
No gate-calibration details or error bars; the 10 K anomaly explanation is unchanged.
The baseline is now the measured 10 K threshold, but the quantum-capacitance assumptions, uncertainties and field choice are unchanged.
Expansion now attributed to field-induced confinement, and Landau-level origin of oscillations discussed, but only qualitatively.
States that high Delta confines electrons to the MoSe2 layer nearer the WSe2.
Still 1 mV excitation with no amplitude-dependence check.
No light-intensity series added.
Fig. 4 caption no longer claims a sign change in both Rxy and Rxy,drag below 8 K.
Line-cut voltage now quoted as -0.08 V and the cross-device comparison sentence removed.
Trion regions are shaded on the Hall-density plot, but the data gap near Vg = 0 is not stated.
The unsupported claim is removed and replaced by a Lifshitz-Kosevich mass analysis.
Still 0.8 meV at 4 T with mh = 0.45 m0.
Methods no longer describes the flakes by solid lines, but the caption still says 'bottom gate (red line)' against dashed red lines in Methods.
The Rxy colour scale still spans plus or minus 10 kOhm.
Rxy,drag still shown from 2 K and Rxy from 1.5 K.
No channel dimensions added.
Old ED Fig. 7 was removed; its content moved into Fig. 2b,c.
All three Methods typos corrected.

unaddressed_major.title: Hall components not shown to be isolated from huge Rxx
unaddressed_major.why: Antisymmetrization is a standard referee request and easy to answer in a letter; the text still notes Hall values are unreliable where Rxx diverges, so a figure-free answer is plausible.

unaddressed_major.title: Interlayer leakage not characterized
unaddressed_major.why: The group's earlier papers on the same devices characterized leakage, and the only new text is that tunnelling is ignored in the model.

unaddressed_major.title: Gate calibration and 10 K Hall-density anomaly
unaddressed_major.why: The calibration text and the 'weak anomaly' wording are unchanged, which suggests no referee pressed on it.
